clue.text: Disciple at back of church with a new piece to sing

indicators.note: the disciple comes after, at the rear of, the church, a and new pieces

parts.note: a disciple is a follower, figuratively a son of the master

explanation.surface: A follower stands at the back of the church holding a new piece of music to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: A son is a follower or disciple in the old sense, as in 'sons of the prophets'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanson is a French song, a piece of music written for singing.

clue.text: Joining firm, Gregory perhaps makes a bit of money

indicators.note: the actor's surname links up with, follows, the firm

parts.note: Gregory Peck, the Hollywood actor, is an example of a Peck

explanation.surface: Gregory signing up with a company earns himself a little cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A copeck (kopek) is a Russian coin, a hundredth of a rouble, so a small piece of money.

clue.text: A slippery character said to have temper

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the phrase is heard as the answer

explanation.surface: A slippery customer is reported to have a short fuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' reads as anger, but it is the metalworking verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To anneal metal or glass is to heat and cool it slowly to toughen it, which is to temper it.

clue.text: Flower under hidden desk

indicators.note: in a down answer the river sits below the hidden piece

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Aire is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A bloom tucked beneath a secret writing desk.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower is the crossword's river, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretaire is a writing desk with a drop front, often with a cabinet above.

clue.text: Set up a metal device helping irrigation

indicators.note: in a down answer the letters are raised, reading from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Install a metal device to help water the crops.
explanation.definitionFit: A noria is a water wheel with buckets that lifts water into irrigation channels.

clue.text: Belligerent husband and wife outside a very old city

indicators.note: husband and wife stand either side of the a, enclosing it

parts.note: Kish was an ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A warlike married couple are camped outside an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: Kish, near Babylon, is one of the oldest recorded cities.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawkish describes someone favouring war or aggressive policy, which is to be belligerent.

clue.text: Hotel with a bar has times for dances

parts.note: to bar is to ban, prohibit

explanation.surface: A hotel with a bar keeps evenings free for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Habaneras are slow Cuban dances in duple time, named after Havana.

clue.text: Open country with earth, no river

indicators.note: with no river means the river is taken out of the earth

explanation.surface: Open landscape with soil but no stream running through it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wold is an area of high open uncultivated land, as in the Cotswolds.

clue.text: Daft things I see, briefly going round island

indicators.note: the shortened see wraps around the island
the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: I notice silly things in passing while travelling round an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, but it is the bishop's see.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiocies are foolish acts or remarks, the plural of idiocy, stupidity.

clue.text: Protestant suffering enough, but without hint of bitterness

indicators.note: the letters are in a bad way, so they are rearranged
the word but must do without the letter that follows
only the first letter of bitterness is meant, a mere trace

explanation.surface: A Protestant has endured plenty, yet bears no grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting surface: the Huguenots were persecuted French Protestants.
explanation.definitionFit: The Huguenots were French Calvinists, a Protestant community persecuted in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

clue.text: Fear of deity in charge

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: Dread of a god who is in control.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting, since panic is named after Pan, whose shout was said to terrify.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, so the noun works as a synonym.

clue.text: Up and about, crying like a frenzied animal

definitions.note: to be up, as in up in arms, is to be in revolt

parts.note: a stag in rut bells, giving a loud roaring cry

explanation.surface: Someone out of bed and moving around, howling like a crazed beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up and about' reads as one phrase meaning out of bed, but it splits after 'Up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Up in the sense of risen against authority matches rebelling, rising in revolt.

clue.text: Mistress shifted cheat, one getting in the way

indicators.note: the letters of cheat are moved around into a new order
one enters the way, sitting inside it

parts.note: a lane is a way or road
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A scheming mistress relocated a swindler who was obstructing her.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatelaine is the mistress of a large house or castle, keeper of its keys.

clue.text: Spots what sounds like East End carriage?

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word pronounced the way the carriage is said

parts.note: a hackney is a horse-drawn carriage for hire, and Hackney is in London's East End, where the H is dropped

explanation.surface: Spotting what seems to be a Cockney cab.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney drops the initial H, so a hackney carriage is spoken as ''ackney'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition producing pimples, so a crop of spots.

clue.text: Twisted colon? Doubt doctor will make a note of this

definitions.text: doctor will make a note of this

indicators.note: a twisted colon is contorted, so its letters with the next word's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient fears a twisted bowel, and the doctor will record a test result.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood count is a measurement of the cells in a blood sample, which a physician records.

clue.text: Observe as oil splashed round in artistic style

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about and scattered into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Watch as oil paint is splattered about in an arty manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Basso-relievo, low relief, is a sculptural technique where figures project slightly from the background.

clue.text: Fuddy-duddy individual in revisited starting place?

parts.note: a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person

explanation.surface: An old fogey on his own going back to where he began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back to square one' means returning to the start, so the question mark marks a place revisited.
explanation.definitionFit: Square one is the start point to which one returns after failure, from the idiom back to square one.

clue.text: Offer of support given to very big gangster?

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
Al Capone was the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: Backing extended to a huge mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags Al as an example of a gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is something put forward for consideration, a suggestion or offer.

clue.text: Saying a solid figure should be put outside small house

indicators.note: the solid figure is to be placed around the small house

parts.note: a prism is a geometric solid
HO is an abbreviation of house; small signals the shortening

explanation.surface: A rule that a solid shape must stand outside a little home.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphorism is a pithy saying expressing a general truth.

clue.text: Consequence of engineers attending noisy instruments?

indicators.note: the engineers come with, alongside, the instruments, placed first

parts.note: percussion instruments are the drums, cymbals and so on that are struck

explanation.surface: The fallout from army engineers turning up with the drum kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A repercussion is an after-effect or result of some action, often unwelcome.

clue.text: Volume measurement of reduced sound from all sides?

parts.note: a stere is a cubic metre, used for timber

indicators.note: the word of is cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Measuring the volume of quieter all-round sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests loudness, but it is the space measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Stereo sound comes from two or more speakers, giving a spatial, surrounding effect.

clue.text: Cared-for children initially here possibly?

indicators.note: the letters could be arranged another way, giving the answer
only the opening letters of Cared-for and children are used

explanation.surface: Perhaps this is where children are looked after.
explanation.definitionFit: A creche is a nursery where young children are minded while their parents work.

clue.text: Something extremely small and round implanted into leg

indicators.note: the round shape is set inside the leg like a graft

explanation.surface: A tiny circular object has been surgically inserted into someone's leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A pion is a subatomic particle, a meson, so very tiny indeed.

clue.text: Legal officer favouring region that's kept for top people

indicators.note: the region holds the top people inside it

parts.note: a sector is a region or zone

explanation.surface: A lawyer who supports an area reserved for the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosecutor is the official who brings criminal cases to court on behalf of the state.

clue.text: Speedier cooking with no unusual pie for special meal

indicators.note: cooking means being worked on, so the letters of speedier are mixed
with no tells us to take out the letters of pie, and unusual says they need not be in order

explanation.surface: Quicker cooking without an odd pie for a special dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P, I and E from the letters of SPEEDIER and rearrange the remaining SEEDR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seder is the ritual Passover feast held in Jewish homes.

clue.text: One half of double act was bad; missing sidekick, ultimately

indicators.note: the past tense loses the letter from the sidekick
only the final letter of sidekick is meant

explanation.surface: A comedy partner was dreadful without his foil, in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan Laurel was one half of the comic duo Laurel and Hardy.

clue.text: Second criminal isn't being imprisoned, showing such good character

indicators.note: the isn't is locked up inside the second and the criminal

parts.note: a hood is a hoodlum, a gangster
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A second offender is not being jailed, which shows what a fine character he is.
explanation.definitionFit: Sainthood is the state of being a saint, marked by exceptional virtue.

clue.text: Like some language that's horrible mostly and preposterous mostly

indicators.note: most of the word for horrible is kept, its final letter lost

parts.note: ugh is the exclamation at something horrible

indicators.note: again most of the word is kept, this time the word for preposterous, losing its end

parts.note: 'that's rich' is said of a preposterous claim

explanation.surface: Describing a tongue that is mostly awful and mostly absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'mostly's mean the word loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugric is the branch of the Finno-Ugric family including Hungarian, so it describes certain tongues.

clue.text: Plates of a meal scattered about at home

indicators.note: the scattered letters go round, enclosing, the at-home piece
the letters of a meal are strewn about into a new order

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Crockery from a dinner left lying all over the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Laminae are thin layers or scales, the plural of lamina, a thin plate of material.

clue.text: Den in city that's defaced in part

indicators.note: the damaged city sits inside the part

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

indicators.note: the city loses its face, its first letter

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England

explanation.surface: A lair in a city whose buildings have been vandalised in places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In part' looks like 'partly', but 'part' is the role that holds the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A rathole is a squalid, cramped place, a den in the disparaging sense.
